subject: How to find appropriate initial values for IPM

messages.author: ae0d0faac04406b4
messages.subject: How to find appropriate initial values for IPM
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to run an integrated population model combining CMR and point-count data.  
I have set up a multi-state model for the CMR data to get survival estimates (by site, age and origin of birds - here is a discussion about the CMR model I'm using) and I have a N-mixture model to estimate total abundance on each site (quite basic with detection as a linear relationship with several covariates and a random effect). 
The matrix population model I use is a 2-age classes for wild individuals and also releases individuals, following the study of Sarrazin & Legendre 2000 (Conserv. Biol. 14). 
A particularity of our model is that point-counts occur in March and releases in September. Thus, I built "seasonal" matrix population model with 2 intervals: Spring(y) to Autumn(y) and Autumn(y) to Spring(y+1).
For each site, I can estimate total abundance (NTot) as the sum of abundance at each spatial replicate (N.rep) from the N-mixture model. The total abundance is also the sum of the 3 classes (juv and ad wild individuals + releases). To deal with that, and because I could not define twice total abundance, the trick was to use a multinomial distribution for the abundance of each replicate:
N.rep[i,a,s] ~ dmulti(pi[i,s],NTot[a,s])
NTot[a,s] <- N[1,a,s]+N[2,a,s]+N[3,a,s] #N1, N2 and N3 are number of wild subadults, wild adults and releases subadults respectively
I figured out how to write the model and it's ok for JAGS. The model can be compiled, so, it's a first good point.
The tricky part now is to find good initial values. When running the N-mixture model alone, I used the maximum number of observed individuals as initial values and it works.
However, now, with the new constraints on N.rep (that must also satisfy to constraint associated with the population model), I'm quite stuck to find proper initial values for N.rep... 
I have tried several initials values, from the max of observed ind to the real abundance at each replicate, but none is working. 

If you have any idea or general tips on how to provide "good" initials values ...

Thanks for the help !

Guillaume

messages.author: 2663fa87b2cb2117
messages.subject: Re: How to find appropriate initial values for IPM
parts:
Guillaume,


I ran my IPM through WinBUGS. When it crashed, I chose Model -> Save State. Then I copy and pasted the values used in the sampler, and specified those as inits, and ran the model again. For my issue, the sampler would run a bit, but then crash, but usually one or two of the three chains were alright, just one of them hung things up. So I looked at the three windows with the final values from each chain and made sure not to use the chain with extreme values for the inits.


Seemed to work for me. Then I could transfer those working inits and run in JAGS or whatever other program that may be desirable. Not sure if JAGS has a similar 'save state' option (would assume it does)?


I can't speak to the whether this is theoretically appropriate, but it seemed to produce reasonable results.


Hope this helps a bit!


Andrew
